quiz.q: According to Locke, what is the primary outcome of the first social contract compared to the second?
options: The first contract surrenders all natural rights, while the second contract selects an absolute sovereign.
The first contract creates civil society, while the second contract establishes a limited government.
The first contract establishes an elected legislature, while the second contract institutes the judicial system.
The first contract dissolves the state of nature, while the second contract creates an unregulated market.
quiz.why: Locke's first contract forms civil society where people recognize each other's rights, whereas the second contract creates government as a trust.

quiz.q: On what philosophical ground did John Locke refute Robert Filmer's defense of absolute hereditary monarchy?
options: Paternal authority over dependent children differs fundamentally from political authority over rational and equal citizens.
Hereditary succession is valid only when ratified by a unanimous vote of all property-owning subjects.
Monarchs derive legitimate absolute power from a single social contract rather than direct divine inheritance.
Filmer failed to recognize that kings must exercise absolute authority through a formalized legislative assembly.
quiz.why: Locke argued that paternal rule over dependent children cannot justify political authority over citizens, who are rational and free equals.

quiz.q: Why does C. B. Macpherson characterize John Locke's political theory as possessive individualism?
options: Locke asserts that all private property must eventually be surrendered to the state for collective welfare.
Locke demands that economic wealth be redistributed equally among all citizens through progressive tax policies.
Locke argues that property ownership is a collective communal entitlement rather than an individual moral right.
Locke justifies absolute property rights and assumes individuals owe no social obligation to give back to society.
quiz.why: Macpherson argued that Locke defends bourgeois interests by treating property as personal achievement without any social obligation to society.

quiz.q: What does the right to revolution mean in John Locke's theory of limited government?
options: A violent insurrection by the working class to abolish private property and overthrow the state apparatus.
A permanent dissolution of both civil society and government, returning citizens to the state of nature.
A peaceful constitutional change of rulers through elections when the government breaches its delegated trust.
An automatic executive suspension of the legislature whenever citizens disagree on the enforcement of natural laws.
quiz.why: For Locke, revolution does not mean violent destruction of society, but a peaceful constitutional replacement of rulers who breach trust.
